crawlmouse.heading: Paste a URL. Get an honest grade.
crawlmouse.tagline: Crawlmouse grades how well your website's pages link to each other — the thing that decides whether Google and AI tools like ChatGPT can actually find your content — and shows you exactly what to fix. 250+ audits run across nearly 200 sites.

features.title: A–F internal-linking grade
features.body: Calibrated bands, not vibes. Same site, same answer, every time.

features.title: AI-readiness score
features.body: Audits the static HTML that GPTBot, Claude, and Perplexity actually read. If AI crawlers can't see your content, you'll know.

features.title: Orphan pages & click depth
features.body: Every page nothing links to, and every page buried too deep to matter.

features.title: Prioritized findings
features.body: Severity and the percentage of pages affected on every issue, so you fix what matters first.

features.title: Honest limits
features.body: When a site can't be measured properly — too small, blocked, JavaScript-only shell — Crawlmouse says so instead of inventing a grade. A tool that admits what it can't see is a tool you can trust.

audience: Built for site owners, marketers, and agencies who want the truth about their site structure without a sales call attached.

hafsaSastho.heading: Healthcare guidance in the language mothers actually speak.
hafsaSastho.tagline: Hafsa Sastho is an AI-powered maternal and infant health companion built in Bangla, for Bangladesh — vaccine schedules, growth tracking, and everyday guidance for the first years of a child's life. 80 beta testers use it daily.

features.title: Hafsa Apa
features.body: The AI companion new mothers name first in their feedback. She answers everyday health questions in plain Bangla, day or night, with the patience of an older sister. (“Apa” means elder sister.)

features.title: Vaccine schedule
features.body: Bangladesh's EPI immunization calendar, tracked per child, with reminders.

features.title: Works offline
features.body: Built for real network conditions, not ideal ones.

audience: Built because of a real gap — millions of mothers navigate pregnancy and infancy with no accessible guidance in their own language. This is our answer. It's also how we prove we build AI for real users in hard conditions, not just demos.

storyParagraphs: Nahl (نحل) is Arabic for honeybee — small, relentless, and useful far beyond its size.

Nahl Technologies was started by two immigrants who came to the United States with little more than a plan to learn. Udaay Sikder earned his BS and MS in Computer Science here and has spent his career in the tech industry; Mohieminul Khan earned his PhD in Mechanical Engineering and brings five years of industry experience. One of us builds software; the other builds systems. Together, that's the point.

We're proudly based in Indiana and we work with businesses everywhere — across the United States and around the world — helping them adopt AI and put it to work. We build with AI in every part of our own operation; it isn't a service we bolted on, it's how the company runs. The products we've shipped, the research we publish, and this website itself are the proof we'd rather show than tell.
The American dream, as far as we can tell, still works. You just have to build it.
